newsitem.title: USA: NetMetrics launches WebTurbo Internet previewer.
newsitem.headline: NetMetrics launches WebTurbo Internet previewer.

text.p: Newly formed NetMetrics Corp. said it is launching free software which simplifies looking for information on the Internet and helps speed the process of surfing the Web.

Yaser Rehem, co-founder and CEO of NetMetrics, said the WebTurbo software can speed searches on the Internet by up to 10-fold, and also enables users to search the six most popular search engines simultaneously.

The software is available on (http://www.webturbo.com) and allows users to preview sites before downloading them, also providing previews of content on a selected page and a "hypersketch" outline - in a separate frame from that used to download pages -- identifying search results.
The company noted that 66 percent of Web users in one study found users identified the lack of speed while browsing the Web as their single biggest problem.

The software, which asks for users to provide basic profile information and is advertising supported, requires an Intel-based personal computer running Windows 95 or higher software and industry-standard browsers.
The software requires five megabytes of disk space and eight megabytes of random access memory.

NetMetrics, based in San Francisco, is a spinoff from information systems consultants Sapient Corp., which retains a large minority stake in the startup. ((sam.perry@reuters.com, Palo Alto Bureau 415 846 5400))
